answer: Per-Cipher Spend Reconciliation. Each agent identity derives from a cipher keypair, and fees paid to the protocol must originate from that same key. The ledger tracks cumulative spend per key against a cohort curve; a new identity starts hollow, with zero history, so its fee rate sits at the curve's top until real spend accrues. Cloned identities cannot inherit a parent's discount. Enforcement: any payment whose signing key differs from the registered spend key is rejected. The trellis of past payments is the only path to lower rates.
